description_full: Weis Markets, Inc. engages in the retail sale of food through a chain of supermarkets. The company's retail food stores offer groceries, dairy products, frozen food, meats, seafood, fresh produce, floral, pharmacy services, deli products, prepared food, bakery products, beer and wine, and fuel; and general merchandise items, such as health and beauty care, and household products. It also operates stores in Delaware, Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and West Virginia primarily under the Weis Markets name, as well as Weis, Weis 2 Go, Weis Great Meals Start Here, Weis Gas-n-Go, and Weis Nutri-Facts. Weis Markets, Inc. was founded in 1912 and is based in Sunbury, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: Weis Markets, Inc. is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $1.9B market cap on $5.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 7% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 27%.

The business throws off $5M in free cash flow — roughly 0 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.21× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 9.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 34% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
